nodes.title: Design review of the app as released (release 16, int/r6 integration 24), by the main loop from pixels: n = 179 screens at each of phone 360x740 and desktop 1366x768, captured by a Sonnet agent with a faked API and a simulated child; facts counted by grep over all CSS: 3 token systems live (classic, v3, Kaksha), 351 distinct hex colours, 69 font-size values, 44 corner radii, 36 CSS files. Judged faults in order of cost: (1) the teacher's face is a big-eyed toddler cartoon and the largest thing on home and lesson; (2) the board is thin white strokes and monospace one-line fractions in a mostly empty frame; (3) the chrome is terminal-styled (slash-labels, grid, clipped corners, mono uppercase), and the parent corner was built dark against DESIGN-V3; (4) the question is not the strongest element on the phone lesson screen (seven stacked zones); (5) three designs live at once; (6) broken-looking states (blank white offline home, empty stage boxes). Kept: the desktop lesson structure, the games' blueprint look, the parent corner's content, no streaks or points. This is one reviewer's judgement of stills; no child or parent was asked, and motion and audio were not seen.

The UI revamp goes ahead in two phases. Phase 1 now: a design session builds two directions as static prototypes of eight screens at two sizes (A 'paper and ink': warm light ground, the board as paper, marigold and indigo; B 'night class': the current dark calmed, terminal affectations removed) and one page comparing current, A and B for the owner. Phase 2 after the owner picks: one token set (at most 8 type sizes, 3 radii, under 30 colours), then the lesson screen and board, home, onboarding, the parent corner (light), and the classic skin retired. Fixed in both directions, not taste: the board is the hero and maths is typeset as maths with colour carrying meaning; the question is the second strongest element with one primary action; the teacher is a small presence, never the hero image (the owner chooses the teacher's look separately); no slash-labels, grid, clipped corners or chevrons; every state has a designed fallback. Why: the owner called the UI extremely bad on 2026-11-10 having seen only the October build, then left the call to the main loop; the review of the current build (ms-r8-design-review-2026-11-10) found three of October's faults still present and one new one; the look is taste, so the owner picks from pixels rather than from a description. Reverse if: the owner, having used release 16, says the current look is acceptable (then only the non-taste fixes are built on the current skin); or neither direction is picked (then a third is drawn from the owner's stated reasons before any product code changes).

md.measurements:
## `ms-r8-design-review-2026-11-10` (2026-11-10)

A design review of the app as released (release 16), by the main loop from pixels.

- **n:** 179 screens at each of two sizes (phone 360 × 740, desktop 1366 × 768), captured with a faked API and a simulated child.
- **Counted over all CSS:** 3 token systems live, 351 distinct hex colours, 69 font-size values, 44 corner radii, 36 CSS files.
- **Judged faults, in order of cost:** the teacher's toddler-cartoon face as the largest thing on home and lesson; the board as thin strokes and monospace one-line fractions in a mostly empty frame; terminal-styled chrome, with the parent corner built dark; the question not the strongest element on the phone lesson screen; three designs live at once; broken-looking states (a blank white offline home).
- **Kept:** the desktop lesson structure, the games' look, the parent corner's content.

**Limits:** one reviewer's judgement of stills. No child or parent was asked. Motion and audio were not seen.

Full write-up: docs/design/round8/DESIGN-REVIEW.md.
md.decisions:
## `dc-r8-design-revamp-two-directions` (2026-11-10)

The UI revamp goes ahead in two phases.

- **Phase 1, now:** two directions as static prototypes of eight screens at two sizes, and one page comparing current, A and B for the owner. A is "paper and ink" (warm light ground, the board as paper). B is "night class" (the current dark, calmed).
- **Phase 2, after the owner picks:** one token set, then the lesson screen and board, home, onboarding, the parent corner (light), and the classic skin retired.

**Fixed in both directions:** the board is the hero and maths is typeset as maths; the question is the second strongest element; the teacher is a small presence, never the hero image; no slash-labels, grid, clipped corners or chevrons; every state has a designed fallback.

**Why:** the owner called the UI extremely bad having seen only the October build, then left the call to the main loop. The review of the current build found three of October's faults still present and one new one. The look is taste, so the owner picks from pixels.

**Reverse if:**
- the owner, having used release 16, says the current look is acceptable: only the non-taste fixes are built, on the current skin;
- neither direction is picked: a third is drawn from the owner's stated reasons before any product code changes.
